title: Perfectness is invariant under changing the derived localization universe
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let two choices of its derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] have arbitrary, independently chosen morphism universes. The canonical equivalence obtained by uniqueness of localization preserves and reflects perfectness [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. More precisely it preserves the actual bounded finite-projective representing cochain complex and both bounds: only its marking in the chosen localization changes.

source.place: Tag 05RU, derived category as localization; uniqueness of localization. Applied to the perfect representative in more-algebra.tex Tag 09AW when transporting its reconstruction to the standard localization in proetale.tex Tag 09C5.

proof.text: Let E be the canonical equivalence between the two localization functors Q1 and Q2. Mathlib Localization.compUniqFunctor supplies Q1⋙E.functor≅Q2, and Localization.compUniqInverse supplies Q2⋙E.inverse≅Q1. If K≅Q1(P) is a bounded finite-projective marking, apply E.functor and its comparison to obtain E(K)≅Q2(P). Conversely, from E(K)≅Q2(P), compose the equivalence unit at K, E.inverse applied to the marking, and the inverse comparison at P. The same P, degree bounds, and projective finite terms prove both directions of [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex].

theorem isPerfectRingComplex_change_localization_iff {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (h₁ : HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} (ModuleCat.{u} R))
    (h₂ : HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} (ModuleCat.{u} R))
    (K : @DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) _ _ h₁) :
    @IsPerfectRingComplex R _ h₂
        ((Localization.uniq
          (@DerivedCategory.Q (ModuleCat.{u} R) _ _ h₁)
          (@DerivedCategory.Q (ModuleCat.{u} R) _ _ h₂)
          (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso _ (.up ℤ))).functor.obj K) ↔
      @IsPerfectRingComplex R _ h₁ K
